easy.def: Something you do all the time without thinking.
examples: Brushing my teeth is a habit.
Biting your nails is a bad habit.
She has a habit of humming.

more.def: Something you do so often that you do it without thinking.
examples: Brushing your teeth is a good habit.
He has a habit of biting his nails.

easy.def: The place where an animal or plant lives.

more.def: The natural home of a plant or animal, where it finds what it needs to live.

easy.def: The way your hair is cut and arranged.

No harm was done by the spill.
Too much sun can cause harm to your skin.

easy.def: To hurt or damage.
examples: Do not harm the bird.
The frost harmed the plants.
It will not harm you.

more.def: To hurt or damage someone or something.
examples: Do not harm the animals.
The frost harmed the young plants.
Gentle play will not harm the puppy.

easy.def: Able to hurt you or make you sick.
examples: Too much sun can be harmful.
Some plants are harmful.
Smoke is harmful to the air.

more.def: Able to cause damage, injury or illness.
examples: Too much sun can be harmful to your skin.
Some mushrooms are harmful if you eat them.
Litter can be harmful to wild animals.

easy.def: Not able to hurt anyone.
examples: The snake is harmless.
The spider is harmless.
The joke was harmless.

more.def: Not likely to cause harm or hurt.
examples: The garden snake is harmless.
The dog looks big but is harmless.
It was a harmless joke.

easy.def: A small instrument that you play by blowing into it.
examples: He plays the harmonica.
The harmonica is small.
I blew the harmonica.

more.def: A small musical instrument that you hold to your mouth and play by blowing and drawing air through holes.
examples: He played a tune on his harmonica around the campfire.
A harmonica is small enough to fit in your pocket.
The cowboy in the story played a sad song on the harmonica.

easy.def: Getting along well.
examples: The class works in harmony.
The two groups live in harmony.
We live in harmony.

more.def: A peaceful state in which people agree and get along.
examples: The class works together in harmony.
The two towns lived in harmony.
Neighbors of every kind lived in harmony.

easy.def: Musical notes that sound good together.
examples: The choir sang in harmony.
The harmony is lovely.
She sings harmony.

more.def: Different musical notes that are played or sung together to make a pleasing sound.
examples: The singers blended in harmony.
The two girls sang a sweet harmony.
The song has a rich harmony.

easy.def: Straps that hold a horse to a cart or keep you safe.
examples: The horse wears a harness.
The dog's harness is red.
The climber wore a harness.

more.def: A set of straps used to hold something in place, to control an animal, or to keep a person safe.
examples: The horse pulled the cart in its leather harness.
The climber clipped her harness to the rope.
My dog wears a harness on walks.

easy.def: To use the power of something.
examples: We harness the wind.
They harnessed the river.
She harnessed her energy.

more.def: To control something and use its power.
examples: Wind turbines harness the power of the wind.
The village harnessed the river to turn a mill.
She harnessed her energy to finish the project.

easy.def: A big music maker with strings you pull with your fingers.
examples: She plays the harp.
The harp is big.
The harp makes soft music.

more.def: A large musical instrument with many strings that you pluck with your fingers.
examples: She plays the harp in the school orchestra.
The harp made soft, gentle music.
An angel in the painting played a golden harp.

easy.def: Rough and unpleasant.
examples: The harsh wind blew.
A harsh voice.
The light is harsh.

more.def: Rough and unpleasant to feel, hear or see.
examples: The harsh wind stung our faces.
He spoke in a harsh voice.
The harsh light hurt my eyes.

easy.def: To pick food that has grown.
examples: We harvest corn from the field.
We harvest pumpkins in the fall.
The farmer harvests the wheat.

more.def: To gather crops when they are ripe and ready.
examples: Farmers harvest apples in the fall.
We harvested tomatoes from our garden all summer.
Workers harvest the grapes by hand.

related.def: A person or machine that gathers crops.

easy.def: A food made of chopped meat and potatoes cooked together.
examples: We had hash for dinner.
The hash is hot.
Mom cooked hash.

more.def: A dish of cooked meat and potatoes that are chopped up and fried together.
examples: We had corned beef hash for breakfast.
The hash was served with a fried egg.
Grandpa cooked hash in a big pan.

easy.def: The symbol # on a keyboard or phone.
examples: Press the hash key.
The hash is a symbol.
Type a hash.

more.def: A symbol that looks like a tic-tac-toe grid (#), used on keyboards, phones and in social media.
examples: Press the hash key to end the number.
The hash symbol is above the number three on the keyboard.
She put a hash before the word in her post.

easy.def: Something that is a bother.
examples: It is a hassle to wait.
Packing is a hassle.
I do not want a hassle.

more.def: Something that is annoying or a lot of trouble.
examples: It is a hassle to pack for a long trip.
Waiting in the long line was a big hassle.
I did not want the hassle of cleaning the whole house.

easy.def: To keep bothering someone.
examples: Do not hassle your brother.
He hassled me.
She hassles her friend.

more.def: To bother or annoy someone again and again.
examples: Do not hassle your sister while she is reading.
The mosquitoes hassled us all through the picnic.
He hassled his brother until he gave him a turn.

easy.def: Doing something very fast.
examples: In haste, I forgot my hat.
She left in haste.
Haste makes waste.

more.def: A great hurry, or the act of doing something too quickly.
examples: In my haste to leave, I forgot my lunch.
She packed her bag in haste.
Haste can lead to mistakes.

easy.def: In a rush.
examples: He hastily packed.
She hastily ate.
They hastily left.

more.def: Quickly, in a hurry and without much care.
examples: He hastily packed his bag.
She hastily wrote a note.
They hastily left when it started to rain.

easy.def: Too fast, without thinking.
examples: He made a hasty choice.
A hasty trip.
The hasty answer was wrong.

more.def: Done too quickly and without enough care.
examples: He made a hasty choice and picked the wrong one.
We made a hasty trip to the store.
The hasty answer on the test turned out to be wrong.

easy.def: Something you wear on your head.
examples: Wear a hat.
His hat is red.
The sun hat is big.

more.def: A covering that you wear on your head.
examples: She wore a straw hat to keep off the sun.
He pulled his wool hat over his ears.
A tall hat sat on the clown's head.

easy.def: To break out of an egg.
examples: The chick will hatch.
The eggs hatched.
The baby turtle hatched.

more.def: To come out of an egg, or to make a baby come out of an egg.
examples: The chicks hatched on Monday.
Sea turtle eggs hatch on the beach.
The hen sat on the eggs until they hatched.

easy.def: A small ax with a short handle.
examples: Dad used a hatchet.
The hatchet is sharp.
He split wood with a hatchet.

more.def: A small ax with a short handle that is held in one hand, used for chopping wood.
examples: Dad used a hatchet to chop kindling for the campfire.
The hatchet is a tool that must be used carefully.
A hatchet hung on the wall of the shed.

easy.def: To not like something at all.
examples: I hate peas.
She hates the cold.
He hated losing.

more.def: To dislike someone or something very strongly.
examples: I hate it when my socks get wet in the rain.
My brother hates loud noises.
She hated saying goodbye to her friends.

easy.def: Full of meanness or hate.
examples: That was a hateful thing to say.
A hateful look.
Hateful words hurt.

more.def: Full of hate, or very mean and unkind.
examples: It was hateful to call someone a bad name.
The hateful words hurt her feelings.
In the story, the hateful stepsister was jealous.

easy.def: Very strong dislike.
examples: He felt hatred.
The hatred was strong.
Hatred is not kind.

more.def: A very strong feeling of dislike for someone or something.
examples: He felt hatred for the bully.
The villain's hatred grew.
Hatred makes problems worse.

easy.def: To pull or carry something heavy.
examples: The truck hauls sand.
We hauled the box.
He hauled the bags.

more.def: To carry or drag something heavy from one place to another.
examples: The truck hauled a load of sand.
They hauled the boat up the beach.
She hauled the heavy bags up the stairs.

easy.def: To visit a place as a ghost.
examples: A ghost haunts the house.
The old house is haunted.
The story of the haunting.

more.def: To appear in a place as a ghost in stories, or to stay in your mind.
examples: A ghost haunts the old house in the story.
The haunted castle was empty.
The sad song haunted me all day.

easy.def: To own or hold something.
examples: I have a red ball.
She has two cats.
We had a nice time.

more.def: To own something, to hold it, or to be given or filled with something.
examples: My cousin has a telescope for looking at the stars.
Spiders have eight legs.
We had pancakes for breakfast on Saturday.

easy.def: A big mess and trouble.
examples: The storm caused havoc.
The puppy made havoc in the house.
Havoc broke out at the party.

more.def: Great confusion and damage, with things in disorder.
examples: The strong wind caused havoc in the garden.
The loose puppy created havoc in the kitchen.
Snow caused havoc on the roads this morning.

easy.def: Dried grass that is fed to animals.
examples: The cows eat hay.
The hay is dry.
The barn is full of hay.

more.def: Grass that has been cut and dried so that it can be fed to farm animals.
examples: The horses ate hay in the barn.
The farmer stacked bales of hay.
We jumped into the pile of hay.

easy.def: A ride on a wagon filled with hay.
examples: We went on a hayride.
The hayride was bumpy.
A tractor pulled the hayride.

more.def: A ride for fun on a wagon or truck piled with hay.
examples: We went on a hayride at the pumpkin farm.
The tractor pulled the hayride around the field.
Everyone sang songs on the hayride.

easy.def: A big pile of hay.
examples: A needle in a haystack.
The haystack is tall.
The cat slept in the haystack.

more.def: A large pile of hay stacked outdoors, often in a field.
examples: The cat curled up in the warm haystack.
Looking for the lost key was like looking for a needle in a haystack.
The farmer built a tall haystack in the field.

easy.def: Not working right.
examples: The computer went haywire.
My toy went haywire.
The clock went haywire.

more.def: Not working properly, or out of control.
examples: The clock went haywire and rang at midnight.
The robot toy went haywire and spun in circles.
Our plans went haywire when it started to rain.

easy.def: Something that could cause harm or danger.
examples: A wet floor is a hazard.
The toy on the stairs is a hazard.
Ice is a hazard.

more.def: Something that can cause harm, danger or accidents.
examples: A wet floor can be a hazard, so watch your step.
The sign warned drivers of ice, a hazard on the road.
Loose rocks are a hazard to anyone hiking on the trail.

easy.def: Dangerous.
examples: The ice is hazardous.
A hazardous road.
Hazardous waste.

more.def: Dangerous or risky, so that it could cause harm.
examples: The icy road was hazardous, so we drove slowly.
The sign warned of hazardous chemicals.
Climbing without a rope is hazardous.

easy.def: A thin cloud of dust or smoke in the air.
examples: A haze hung over the hills.
The haze made it hard to see.
We saw haze in the sky.

more.def: A thin mist of dust, smoke or tiny drops of water in the air that makes it hard to see far.
examples: A summer haze covered the valley and hid the far hills.
Haze from the distant fire turned the sun a dull orange.
A morning haze rose from the warm lake.

easy.def: Not clear, like when it is misty.
examples: The sky is hazy.
A hazy day.
The hazy hills were pale.

more.def: Not clear because of mist, smoke or dust in the air.
examples: The hills looked hazy in the morning mist.
A hazy sky hid the sun.
I have a hazy memory of the trip.
